7_1_elementary_ca_vr.name: 7_1_elementary_ca_vr
7_1_elementary_ca_vr.qfep_connection: Eight bits of rule_number are the entire legislature; each new strip of 128 cells is a neighborhood vote on the row above, and the dial exposes all 256 possible laws. That triangles, static, or Rule 30's chaos separate by a single integer is the lesson: F_order this thin still decides everything downstream.

7_2_game_of_life_vr.name: 7_2_game_of_life_vr
7_2_game_of_life_vr.qfep_connection: Room-scale Life where the law is locked and only the seed is yours: a single 'Alive %' dial reseeds the 20×20 field, then B3/S23 spends your disorder deterministically, generation by generation. You legislate nothing — you only decide how much randomness the constitution gets to consume.

7_3_game_of_life_oop_vr.name: 7_3_game_of_life_oop_vr
7_3_game_of_life_oop_vr.qfep_connection: The rebuild hands over what 7_2 withheld: Survive Min, Survive Max, and Birth as three grabbable dials, each cell now an object holding its own state. Conway's constants become sliders — B3/S23 revealed as one point in a rule space you can walk, not a law of nature.

7_8_hexagon_ca_vr.description: hex_cell(t+1) = life_rule(6_neighbors) stacked vertically — terrain from time
7_8_hexagon_ca_vr.name: 7_8_hexagon_ca_vr

CA_sphere.description: vertex(t+1) = evolve(mode, neighbors) where mode in {CA, random_walk, hill_seeking}
CA_sphere.name: CA_sphere

CellularAutomata3DStacked.description: layer(n+1) = life_rules(layer(n)) with outward→upward phase transition
CellularAutomata3DStacked.name: CellularAutomata3DStacked

CellularAutomata3DTree.description: square_layer(n) → ca_prune(edge, isolation, random) → tree silhouette
CellularAutomata3DTree.name: CellularAutomata3DTree

CrosswayCA.description: Each row obeys a different Wolfram rule number. Where rule regimes collide at row boundaries, interference patterns emerge — moire-like zones of order in the chaos. Every 10 turns all rules re-randomize and the entire pattern language shifts. A crossroads of computational grammars where the boundaries become the most interesting places.
CrosswayCA.qfep_connection: Critical lambda — each row is a different lambda value (rule number). The boundaries between rows are the edges of chaos, where different computational regimes interfere and produce emergent structure.
CrosswayCA.capacity: SEE that when different rules collide, the boundaries between them produce more complexity than either rule alone
interactions: observe rule collisions at row boundaries
CrosswayCA.name: CrosswayCA

ca_chair_test.name: CA Chair Test
ca_chair_test.qfep_connection: f_order: the chair grown by rule — furniture as the output of a cellular process, sat-on proof that local rules can build to a human scale.

ca_growth_network.description: Network structure that grows using cellular automata rules, forming organic branching patterns through local neighbor interactions.
ca_growth_network.name: CA Growth Network

ca_screen.description: Screen display that renders live cellular-automata patterns — rule outputs visualised on a flat panel as the simulation runs.
ca_screen.name: CA Screen
ca_screen.qfep_connection: f_order: the rule made watchable — a flat panel rendering a live automaton, generations scrolling as they are computed. The chapter's television: local rules broadcasting their global consequence.

ca_showcase.description: A collection of various cellular automata demonstrations.
ca_showcase.name: CA Showcase
ca_showcase.qfep_connection: Survey of CA behavior classes — each class maps to a λ value. Class I (death) = λ=0, Class II (static) = low λ, Class IV (complex) = λ≈0.4, Class III (chaotic) = λ→1. The full spectrum rendered.

ca_sphere.description: Cellular Automata on a sphere surface.
ca_sphere.name: CA Sphere
ca_sphere.qfep_connection: f_order: an automaton wrapped on a sphere — the same neighborhood rule with no edge to hide at. On a closed surface every cell's consequence eventually comes home.

cellular_automata_1d.name: Cellular Automata 1D
cellular_automata_1d.qfep_connection: Four walls grow Rules 30, 110, 90, and 150 from the identical single-seed start — chaos, universality, fractal lace, and XOR symmetry as north, south, east, west. Enclosed by a controlled experiment, you stand at the middle as its only constant: same input, four elementary futures.

cellular_automata_3d_stacked.name: Cellular Automata 3D Stacked
cellular_automata_3d_stacked.qfep_connection: Time stacked as geometry: 2D automata generations piled into a 3D solid, history become a sculpture. In the fractal rooms it stands as kin evidence — another finite rule whose repetition grows structure across scales.

cellular_automata_3d_tree.name: Cellular Automata 3D Tree
cellular_automata_3d_tree.qfep_connection: f_order: growth as computation — a tree-form accreted by 3D CA steps, branching where the rule permits. The organism as the rule's fossil record.

crack_propagation_ca.description: Simulation of crack propagation in materials.
crack_propagation_ca.name: Crack Propagation CA
crack_propagation_ca.qfep_connection: Three stress points are seeded and never move; every tick they gamble five percent per neighbor, and a cell that cracks stays cracked. Damage here is one-way E_flux — the grid keeps a ledger of every failure and offers no repair rule.

crossway_ca.name: Crossway CA
crossway_ca.qfep_connection: f_order: automata at the crossing — lanes of cells negotiating an intersection by neighborhood rule alone; traffic with no traffic authority.

decaying_bridge.description: A bridge that decays when stepped on.
decaying_bridge.name: Decaying Bridge

dendrite_growth_ca.name: Dendrite Growth CA
dendrite_growth_ca.qfep_connection: Every successful branch is promoted to a growth center, so the frontier itself does the growing — the crystal has no plan, only tips. The line renderer colors cells by birth time, making the structure its own archaeology.

disease_spread_ca.description: SIR model simulation of disease spread.
disease_spread_ca.name: Disease Spread CA
disease_spread_ca.qfep_connection: SIR epidemic dynamics as entropy propagation — infection spreads E(S) through a network, recovery restores local F. The transmission rate IS λ: how fast disorder propagates through structure.

ecosystem_ca.name: Ecosystem CA
ecosystem_ca.qfep_connection: Predation is written as conversion, not deletion: a hunted prey cell is overwritten into a predator. The 'balance of nature' staged here is recruitment — populations regulate each other by rewriting neighbors into their own kind.

elementary_ca_vr.description: 1D Elementary Cellular Automata in VR (Rule 30, etc).
elementary_ca_vr.name: Elementary CA VR
elementary_ca_vr.qfep_connection: Wolfram's 256 rules as a complete λ-spectrum. Rule 30 produces chaos from order, Rule 110 is Turing-complete at the edge of chaos — the simplest system that can compute anything.

game_of_life_oop_vr.description: Object-Oriented Game of Life in VR.
game_of_life_oop_vr.name: Game of Life OOP VR
game_of_life_oop_vr.qfep_connection: Survive-min, survive-max, and birth hang beside the grid as physical sliders, so Conway's 2-3-3 stops being an axiom and becomes a setting within arm's reach. F_order demoted to a knob: the player legislates, then watches the population live or die under the amended rule.

game_of_life_vr.description: Conway's Game of Life in VR.
game_of_life_vr.name: Game of Life VR
game_of_life_vr.qfep_connection: Emergent gliders and oscillators are persistent low-F structures surviving in high-E(S) space. Life exists at Langton's λ ≈ 0.27 — just below the edge of chaos, where complex computation emerges from two rules.

hexagon_ca_vr.description: Cellular Automata on a hexagonal grid.
hexagon_ca_vr.name: Hexagon CA VR
hexagon_ca_vr.qfep_connection: f_order: the same game on six neighbors — a hexagonal lattice showing that 'neighborhood' is a choice, and the choice changes the worlds that can emerge.

hexagon_cave_vr.description: Hexagonal CA generating a cave-like structure with varying radius.
hexagon_cave_vr.name: Hexagon Cave VR
hexagon_cave_vr.qfep_connection: Each CA generation is deposited as a collidable hex layer, so time becomes stratigraphy — a cave you can climb because the automaton refuses to erase its past. The diameter envelope (1m base, 0.4m pinch, 3m crown) admits the negotiation: emergence supplies the texture, a designer's curve supplies the silhouette.

lattice_gas_automata.description: Fluid dynamics simulation using Lattice Gas Automata.
lattice_gas_automata.name: Lattice Gas Automata
lattice_gas_automata.qfep_connection: Discrete particles on a lattice reproducing continuous fluid dynamics — microscopic F (collision rules) generates macroscopic E(S) (turbulence, flow). The Navier-Stokes equations emerge from local interactions.

lenia_continuous.description: Continuous cellular automaton (Lenia) — smooth lifelike organisms emerge from a ring-shaped kernel, bell-curve growth function, and continuous [0,1] states. The 'wow' artifact for cellular automata: watch amorphous blobs self-organize into gliding, pulsing creatures on a glowing floor display.
lenia_continuous.name: Lenia Continuous
lenia_continuous.qfep_connection: Continuous CA with smooth λ-variation. Creatures self-maintain through continuous F-minimization — they persist by predicting their own next state. Lenia lives at the edge of chaos in continuous space.

line_network_ca.description: Base class visualization for line-based cellular automata.
line_network_ca.name: Line Network CA
line_network_ca.qfep_connection: f_order: one-dimensional automata drawn as line networks — the space-time diagram standing up: each generation a stratum, history as geology.

mold_network.name: Mold Network
mold_network.qfep_connection: relation: the slime mold's answer — a network grown by local reinforcement, efficiency without an engineer. The biological cousin of every rule in the room.

percolation_ca.name: Percolation CA
percolation_ca.qfep_connection: Porosity is set a nudge above the critical 0.593, so the seep from the top face is guaranteed yet never attributable to any single cell — crossing is a property of the network, not its members. Criticality as politics: the difference between sealed and leaking is a fraction of a percent of pores.

pulsing_ca.description: Base class visualization for pulsing sphere cellular automata.
pulsing_ca.name: Pulsing CA
pulsing_ca.qfep_connection: Alive means a sphere whose scale rides a sine of time plus its own grid coordinates, so the automaton shimmers in travelling phase waves. Discreteness dressed in continuity — the binary state wears a sinusoid to pass as breathing.

recrystallization_ca.name: Recrystallization CA
recrystallization_ca.qfep_connection: Five random nuclei grow, but all write the same state — the code keeps no record of which seed claimed which cell, so grains meet without boundaries and fuse into one undifferentiated crystal. Order that annexes without borders, distinguished only by a randomized flicker of cyan.

rule_30_110.name: Rule 30/110
rule_30_110.qfep_connection: Rule 30: deterministic chaos (high λ, unpredictable from initial conditions). Rule 110: Turing-complete at λ≈0.4, the exact edge where F-minimization and E(S)-generation balance.

rule_30_110_gravity.name: Rule 30/110 Gravity
rule_30_110_gravity.qfep_connection: lambda_edge: Rule 30 and Rule 110 under gravity — chaos and Turing-completeness made to fall. The two most famous rows of cells in mathematics, given weight.

self_organization_ca.name: Self Organization CA
self_organization_ca.qfep_connection: Self-organization IS F-minimization made visible — local interactions spontaneously produce global order. The system finds its own low-F configuration without external instruction.

sierpinski_pyramid.description: Recursive Sierpinski Pyramid construction using cubes.
sierpinski_pyramid.name: Sierpinski Pyramid
sierpinski_pyramid.qfep_connection: Fractal self-similarity as infinite F-compression — the same pattern at every scale. Sierpinski's triangle emerges from Rule 90 (a CA), showing how recursive structure achieves maximum order with minimum description length.

fold_theatre_runner.description: F-edge first cycle. Substrate runner subclass with all four channels enabled — visibility cycles rule_30 / sierpinski / menger_sponge (the fold vocabulary), glyph runs subdivide_by_attention, part tags via flower_grammar, color-by-role paints concentric flower anatomy. PATH_GUARANTEE keeps spawn-to-teleporter walkable across every visibility pattern. Used by Fold_Theatre in qfeplaboratory.
fold_theatre_runner.name: Fold Theatre Runner

grid_substrate_runner.description: Integrated substrate component — single-cell artifact that mounts visibility (and optionally colour) mutators on the MAP'S existing GridMultiMesh. Same integration shape as gridcolorizer: doesn't build its own multimesh, finds the floor that's already there. Cycles Wolfram CA, fractal, and BFS-frontier expressions on the actual cubes the player walks. Floor-plan SPAWN_LARGEST keeps reachability honest.
grid_substrate_runner.name: Grid Substrate Runner
grid_substrate_runner.qfep_connection: the substrate mount — a single cell that plays rule-patterns through the map's own floor grid; infrastructure that lets the room itself be the automaton, never dominant as an object.

structure_growth.name: Structure Growth
structure_growth.qfep_connection: f_order: architecture accreted cell by cell — a 3D growth simulation where structure is not drawn but reached; the blueprint is the rule, the building is its runtime.

volumetric_fog_ca.description: 3D Cellular Automata driving a volumetric fog.
volumetric_fog_ca.name: Volumetric Fog CA

wireworld_circuit.description: Wireworld cellular automaton — 4-state CA for logic gates and signal routing. Displays an OR gate with clock inputs on a floor display, demonstrating how simple state-transition rules produce computational behavior.
wireworld_circuit.name: Wireworld Circuit
wireworld_circuit.qfep_connection: Computation as signal propagation through constraint — pure F-minimization in a cellular medium. Electrons flow through wire topology; the circuit IS the F-model that channels E(S).

ca_conway_city.name: Conway Emergent City
ca_conway_city.description: Walkable modernist skyline emerging from Conway's Game of Life. B=[3], S=[2,3] run for 10 steps; surviving cells become cubes, height driven by live-neighbor count. No urban planner — the rule is the architect. Change the rule string and the city becomes a different kind of thing.

ca_rule_comparison.name: CA Rule Comparison Garden
ca_rule_comparison.description: Five mini-cities arranged in a cross, each running the same initial density+seed through a different CA rule: Conway B3/S23, HighLife B36/S23, Seeds B2/S, Day-and-Night B3678/S34678, Life-without-Death B3/S012345678. Walking between them teaches rule-sensitivity: the seed is identical, only the acceptance function changed, and the cities are entirely different.

ca_rules_workbench.name: CA Rules Workbench
ca_rules_workbench.description: Interactive 1D Wolfram elementary CA workbench. One slider scrubs rule R in [0,255]; a 256x256 evolution texture redraws live from a single seed cell; class indicator lamp shifts QFEP phase color (Class 1=blue, 2=green, 3=orange, 4=red). Cross-reference labels surface for rules 0/30/54/90/110/126/150/184/254/255 connecting to shannon_workbench, halting_workbench, and (future) fractals galleries. Sister to /ca-rules-gallery (web frieze frozen at 8 highlighted rules).
ca_rules_workbench.gamwell_reference: Wolfram (2002) A New Kind of Science; Cook (2004) proof of rule 110 Turing-completeness.
ca_rules_workbench.qfep_connection: Lambda_edge made into a dial. Wolfram four classes map to QFEP phases: Class 1 (lambda_uniform / frozen), Class 2 (lambda_periodic), Class 3 (lambda_chaotic), Class 4 (lambda_edge). The dial walks rule space; one-bit flips can cross class boundaries.
interactions: grab slider to scrub rule R in [0..255]; evolution texture, class lamp, readout, and cross-reference label update live

parameters.grid_side: Tape width and number of generations (default 256)
parameters.panel_size: Side length of the evolution panel in meters (default 1.0)

elementary_ca_bench.name: Elementary CA Bench (256 universes)
elementary_ca_bench.description: A 1D elementary CA space-time triangle on a bench, cycling the rule number. 256 rules, 256 little universes - the rule is a worldview you can dial.

rule30_bench.name: Rule 30 Bench (order becomes chance)
rule30_bench.description: Rule 30 on a bench, the centre column tinted hot - that column is a bit-stream no shortcut can outrun. Determinism that looks like dice.

rule30_rng.name: Rule 30 RNG (determinism as a dice)
rule30_rng.description: Rule 30 used as a real random-number source: its centre-column bits drive a row of coin cells and a live byte readout. Bridges to the randomness ladder.

rule90_toy.name: Rule 90 Toy (the fractal in the rule)
rule90_toy.description: A held Rule 90 space-time field that IS the Sierpinski triangle - the fractal was hiding in the simplest step.

rule90_bench.name: Rule 90 Bench (Sierpinski forms)
rule90_bench.description: Rule 90 on a bench drawing the Sierpinski gasket generation by generation.

rule90_loom.name: Rule 90 Loom (Sierpinski fabric)
rule90_loom.description: Rule 90 as a textile loom, weaving a scrolling bolt of Sierpinski-patterned cloth - the rule doing a design job.

rule110_bench.name: Rule 110 Bench (gliders)
rule110_bench.description: Rule 110 on a bench - the complex persistent gliders and collisions that make it Turing-complete. Four cells compute anything.

rule110_computer.name: Rule 110 Computer (universal)
rule110_computer.description: Rule 110 framed as a computer: gliders as signals colliding, a UNIVERSAL lamp - origination from a rule that never meant to originate.

life_bench.name: Life Bench (glider gun)
life_bench.description: Conway's Game of Life on a bench with a glider gun streaming gliders. Born on 3, live on 2 or 3 - no designer, only neighbours.

life_zoo_bench.name: Life Zoo Bench (still / pulse / travel)
life_zoo_bench.description: The Game of Life zoo on a bench: a block (still life), a blinker (oscillator), a glider (spaceship), each tinted.

life_rules_room.name: Life Rules Room (a family of laws)
life_rules_room.description: A room of four life-like rules - Conway, HighLife, Seeds, Day&Night - evolving from one shared seed. Life-like is a family, not the law.

brians_brain_bench.name: Brian's Brain Bench (on, fading, off)
brians_brain_bench.description: Three-state Brian's Brain on a bench - on, dying, off - a field that never rests. Perpetual motion from a third state.

brians_brain_display.name: Brian's Brain Display (shimmer screen)
brians_brain_display.description: Brian's Brain as a wall-mounted shimmering display - the dying-state trails used as a generative visual.

wireworld_toy.name: Wireworld Toy (electrons run a loop)
wireworld_toy.description: A held wireworld loop, four states, electron heads and tails chasing around a wire. A universe made of electronics.

wireworld_bench.name: Wireworld Bench (a logic gate)
wireworld_bench.description: A wireworld logic gate on a bench, electrons flowing through it. Four states make wires, and wires make logic.

langton_toy.name: Langton's Ant Toy (held)
langton_toy.description: Langton's ant on a small grid, its black-and-white trail building. Two rules, and after enough steps, a highway.

langton_bench.name: Langton's Ant Bench (the highway)
langton_bench.description: Langton's ant after ten thousand steps - the chaotic core and the emergent highway. Order that arrives only if you wait.

langton_swarm.name: Turmite Swarm (generative paint)
langton_swarm.description: Many turmites painting a shared surface into a generative pattern - simple rules making art.

hex_ca_toy.name: Hex CA Toy (six neighbours)
hex_ca_toy.description: A held hexagonal-grid CA, a six-neighbour rule. Change the shape of nearby and you change what can live.

neighbourhood_bench.name: Neighbourhood Bench (a politics)
neighbourhood_bench.description: The same rule under three neighbourhoods - Moore, von Neumann, hex - making three different worlds. The neighbourhood is a politics.

lenia_room.name: Lenia Room (soft gliders)
lenia_room.description: A room-scale continuous CA on the floor with smooth orbium creatures gliding. Let the cells be fractions, not bits, and life grows soft bodies.

lenia_aquarium.name: Lenia Tank (creature aquarium)
lenia_aquarium.description: Lenia as a creature tank - soft continuous-CA life drifting behind glass. An applied ecosystem display.

reaction_diffusion_bench.name: Reaction-Diffusion Bench (Turing)
reaction_diffusion_bench.description: Gray-Scott on a bench, morphing spots to stripes to maze as F and K drift. Two numbers paint every animal's coat - form from a seed, no blueprint.

lattice_gas_bench.name: Lattice Gas Bench (fluid from cells)
lattice_gas_bench.description: HPP/FHP lattice-gas particles flowing on a bench, coloured by density. Make the cells conserve momentum and the grid becomes a fluid.

lattice_gas_room.name: Lattice Gas Room (flow + obstacle)
lattice_gas_room.description: A room-scale lattice-gas fluid streaming around an obstacle - physics as bookkeeping on a lattice, at walk-in scale.

lattice_gas_pump.name: Lattice Wind Tunnel (vortices)
lattice_gas_pump.description: A lattice-gas wind tunnel: flow past an aerofoil sheds vortices, a live DRAG readout. The CA doing real fluid work.

four_classes_toy.name: Four Classes Toy (held strips)
four_classes_toy.description: Four tiny rule strips, one per Wolfram class - frozen, periodic, chaotic, complex - the fourth tinted as the only live one.

four_classes_bench.name: Four Classes Bench (four weathers)
four_classes_bench.description: The four Wolfram classes side by side, Class 4 glowing. The PCE says they are all the same; the queer reading says only the fourth is alive.

four_classes_room.name: Four Classes Room (the edge is alive)
four_classes_room.description: A room you walk through - frozen, periodic, chaotic, complex - the Class-4 station glowing as the edge where structure persists by moving.

edge_of_chaos_bench.name: Edge of Chaos Bench (lambda dial)
edge_of_chaos_bench.description: A lambda dial sweeps a CA from order through the edge to chaos; the Class-4 band lights up as the sweet spot. Structure persists only by moving.

dendrite_toy.name: Dendrite Toy (DLA crystal)
dendrite_toy.description: Held diffusion-limited aggregation: random-walking particles stick into a branching frost crystal. Structure as frozen history.

dendrite_bench.name: Dendrite Bench (coral growth)
dendrite_bench.description: DLA on a bench growing a coral, particles visibly sticking, coloured by arrival time so the growth history reads.

cave_bench.name: Cave CA Bench (noise to place)
cave_bench.description: Cellular cave generation: random fill, then neighbour-vote smoothing turns noise into a connected walkable cave. Randomness, smoothed into a place.

stigmergy_toy.name: Stigmergy Toy (ant trails)
stigmergy_toy.description: A few ants on a small grid laying an evaporating pheromone trail. The trail is the memory.

stigmergy_bench.name: Stigmergy Bench (self-reinforcing trails)
stigmergy_bench.description: Twenty ants depositing pheromone that evaporates and diffuses, trails self-reinforcing between nest and food. A CA wearing legs.

stigmergy_room.name: Stigmergy Room (slime-mould network)
stigmergy_room.description: A floor-scale ant-colony / slime-mould pheromone network connecting food nodes into paths.

ca_texture_toy.name: CA Texture Toy (frozen swatch)
ca_texture_toy.description: A small CA run to a stable patterned texture tile - a rule frozen as a material swatch.

ca_texture_bench.name: CA Texture Bench (settle to texture)
ca_texture_bench.description: A CA settling toward equilibrium into a repeating textile pattern, with a settling-to-frozen readout. A rule run to equilibrium is a texture.

ca_texture_wall.name: CA Texture Wall (the rug is an algorithm)
ca_texture_wall.description: A wall-scale CA-grown Persian-rug tapestry. The rug is an algorithm that forgot it was ever running.

morpho_egg.name: Morpho Egg (DNA paints a coat)
morpho_egg.description: The held end of the CA->DNA morphogenesis bridge: CritterDNA pattern genes drive a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion that grows the markings on the egg. Same genome, same coat. The CA twin of the seed->form bridge.

morphogenesis_bench.name: Morphogenesis Bench (scrub the coat)
morphogenesis_bench.description: Bench morphogenesis: the pattern gene drifts and the reaction-diffusion coat morphs spots->stripes->maze. The gene-bars are the genome; the markings are downstream. Turing 1952.

morpho_menagerie.name: Morpho Menagerie (one genome, many coats)
morpho_menagerie.description: Room morphogenesis: a lineage of specimens, each an RD coat from the same genome with pattern_type swept 0..1 - the spotted-to-striped continuum is one allele moving.

rule30_random.description: The cellular-automata seam. Rule 30 from one lit cell: its centre column passed the randomness tests and shipped as an RNG, yet it is a fixed rule on a fixed seed - rewind and every bit returns. Determinism wearing randomness.
rule30_random.name: Rule 30 Random
rule30_random.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for cellularautomata. Bias is conserved; show the seam.
